summary: Wiley Post Airport (PWA) is a general aviation facility on the west side of Oklahoma City, named after the legendary Oklahoma-born aviator Wiley Post, who was the first pilot to fly solo around the world and a pioneer of high-altitude flight. The airport primarily serves private, corporate, and recreational aircraft, along with flight training operations, rather than scheduled commercial service. It features multiple runways and is an important reliever airport for the busier Will Rogers World Airport in the Oklahoma City metro area.
faqs:
Q: Does Wiley Post Airport offer commercial airline service?
A: No, Wiley Post is a general aviation airport with no scheduled commercial passenger flights. Travelers should use nearby Will Rogers World Airport (OKC) for commercial service.

Q: Why is the airport named Wiley Post?
A: It honors Wiley Post, an Oklahoma-born aviation pioneer who completed the first solo flight around the world in 1933 and co-developed the first practical pressure suit for high-altitude flying.

Q: What services are available at the airport?
A: The airport hosts fixed-base operators (FBOs) offering fuel, hangar rentals, aircraft maintenance, and flight training schools.

Q: How far is Wiley Post from downtown Oklahoma City?
A: The airport is located roughly 8 miles northwest of downtown Oklahoma City, easily accessible via major roadways including Northwest Expressway.
transport_tips: Renting a car is the most practical way to reach Wiley Post Airport, as there is no public transit directly serving the facility. Ride-share services like Uber and Lyft do operate in the area but availability may be limited. The airport is a short drive from downtown via NW Expressway or the John Kilpatrick Turnpike.
local_tip: Aviation enthusiasts should check out the small display honoring Wiley Post near the terminal area, and consider timing a visit with the airport's annual fly-in events where vintage and homebuilt aircraft are showcased.
